threads.body: [General] This backward-compatibility guarantee is not implemented by the current delegate. `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` wraps these names in `IncludeExclude`, and `CapturedHttpHeaders` then treats `*` and `?` as globs. Now that this PR enables name enumeration, an existing call with the literal name `*` captures every request header; the response, server, and Ratpack aliases have the same problem. Preserve an exact-name path for the deprecated setters before enabling enumeration.

replies.body:
This is exactly the concern the deprecated setters now address, and the exact-name path is already in place — the comment is reading an older snapshot of the base branch.

These deprecated setters no longer build an `IncludeExclude`; they delegate to `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders`, which on this PR's base branch (`trask/http-header-selectors-api`, commit `1572a0077b`) routes through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact` and stores the names as a literal set, with no selector and no glob interpretation. This branch's head commit is simply built on an older snapshot of that base; CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge`, so the literal path is what actually compiles and runs here.

I validated that rather than assuming it: with `1572a0077b` applied locally, the new `doesNotTreatConfiguredNamesAsPatterns` tests in `NettyServerHeaderCaptureTest` and `RatpackServerHeaderCaptureTest` pass, asserting that `setCapturedRequestHeaders(["*"])` and `setCapturedResponseHeaders(["*"])` capture no header attributes at all even though name enumeration is enabled. Those tests exist specifically to pin this behavior so the widening cannot reappear.

Following up with measured evidence rather than leaving this as an assertion, since a stale-base false positive and a real widening would read identically.

I ran the `doesNotTreatConfiguredNamesAsPatterns` regression test both ways, forcing re-execution so nothing came from the build cache.

On the PR merge ref (`refs/pull/19606/merge`, merge commit `5a9c7f8188` of head `9035c9777c` into base `1572a0077b`), which is what CI actually builds, both the Netty and Ratpack tests pass: `setCapturedRequestHeaders(["*"])` and `setCapturedResponseHeaders(["*"])` produce a span with no `http.request.header.*` or `http.response.header.*` attributes at all.

On the head branch in isolation, which is the tree this comment was generated from, the same test fails exactly as described here — the span carries `http.request.header.host=[localhost]`, `http.request.header.x-test-request=[test]`, `http.response.header.x-test-response=[test]` and `http.response.header.content-type=[text/plain]`, i.e. every header. That failure is the base-branch snapshot in this head predating `1572a0077b`, not the code in this diff, and it disappears in the merge.

So the finding is accurate about the widening being dangerous and I've kept a test pinning it, but the fix is present in what merges here.
